name: De Vinne 6pt 1897
designer: Unidentified in the retained source pages
foundry: Shown by the United States Government Printing Office; 1897 stock mark Keystone–10
description: Six-point De Vinne with flared serifs, a sweeping Q tail, double-storey a and g, and observed mixed-height figures. Six named alternates retain source variations.
character_set_notes: Complete observed A–Z, a–z and ten figures, with period, comma and the double-bar historical hyphen encoded as hyphen-minus. Space has a modern layout advance. Six observed alternatives are unencoded glyphs available through stylistic sets; no unsupported character is inferred. 6 whole observed diagonal fractions, cent and percent are also encoded. Fraction row-center placement is a modern layout convention, independent of historical baseline evidence. Unencoded source-quality gaps: U+215B ⅛, U+215C ⅜, U+215D ⅝. The matching poster specimens supply the observed semicolon and right single quotation mark used as an apostrophe; no ASCII apostrophe or opening quotation mark is inferred.
observed: Complete six-point alphabets and figures are observed in both 1897 and census specimens. Matching job-room impressions supply clearer letters, lining five/nine and punctuation. The census M, descending 1897 five/seven/nine and tall job-room zero/one are retained as named alternatives. The document page provides comparison evidence; source-relative figure positions are preserved. Matching ATF assortments supply whole 6-point diagonal fractions and symbols; exact selected pages, crops, thresholds and scale measurements are retained. The three-quarters comes from the matching physical-size seven-labelled BYU assortment; its label and paired native measurements remain explicit. Matching ATF poster specimens supply the whole semicolon and right single quotation mark used as an apostrophe at measured capital scale and native text-row baselines.
reconstructed: No visible form is invented. Uniform source-page scaling, measured rigid baseline rotation, local paper correction and modern spacing prepare the observed forms. No cross-size substitution or independent width stretching. Fraction row-center placement at 350 is a modern layout choice; no historical text baseline is established by the charts. No fraction parts are assembled or redrawn.

revival.author: Harold Lehmann
revival.notes: All visible forms are observed. Four-times Lanczos source sampling preserves small serifs during curve fitting; 71 exact derived crops retain native JP2 coordinates and hashes. Three native pages supply traced forms; the document page is retained for comparison. Uniform page scales and measured row/numeral baseline rotations preserve optical proportions. Six named alternatives use ss01/ss02/ss03. No holes are filled and no visible form is drawn. See source/METHOD.md. The whole fraction companions retain their full physical source dimensions and deliberate slash interruptions. Existing outlines, spacing and named alternatives are preserved. Whole punctuation companions retain observed row-relative positions, independently measured scale and modern 35-unit sidebearings. Exact evidence and quality limits are recorded in source/punctuation-review.json.
